probe_history.reason: Two independently-suggested candidate domains were fetched directly. bassyclub.com returns a live site, but its own retained JSON-LD and <title> ('Virtual Reality im Glücksspiel – Die Zukunft hat begonnen', an online-gambling/VR content article, inLanguage 'en-au') prove it is unrelated third-party content, not Bassy Club Berlin — the domain is not held by the venue. bassy-club.de returns a domain-parking/for-sale template page ('This domain is for sale... Contact the Owner') with an obfuscated tracking/redirect script, not a venue site at all. Neither result is a genuine official first-party presence for the venue, so CANDIDATE_IDENTITY cannot be established from passive discovery of either natural domain guess. Third-party discovery sources (web search results) are themselves in direct conflict about whether the physical club is still operating (a 2018 Tagesspiegel closure report; a Foursquare 'permanently closed' listing; a Yelp listing 'updated July 2026' implying current hours) — none of these are first-party, and none resolve which (if any) domain the venue itself currently controls. Per policy, DEFER does not require exhausting the escalation ladder or fabricating a Level 2/3 probe against a site that has already been shown not to belong to the venue.
